Logan Cooley has 13 points in his last ten games and a fifth career hat trick, which FOX 13 in Utah called NHL history. He's a 9.7 expected-point player over that stretch, so most of it is real. The Mammoth, meanwhile, are 10-7-1 and keep giving games away in net.

This is a good team by process. Utah takes 58 percent of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances), as good as Carolina's, and its shooters score about what they should. The problem is at the other end: the goaltending has allowed nearly 12 more goals than the chances against it predict. Karel Vejmelka has saved 6.0 goals fewer than expected over his last five starts (1-4-0), with a .847 save rate. Sebastian Cossa, with a three-game win streak among his recent starts, looks like the obvious answer for now.

Our race model says Utah has left 2.1 points behind, and our simulations still give the Mammoth an 82 percent playoff chance, because play like this usually wins out. Mikhail Sergachev's point streak and the Anders Lee, Kailer Yamamoto and Barrett Hayton line (75 percent of the chances) show how deep the good stuff runs. If Utah gets league-average saves, this is a team nobody wants to see in the spring.
headline: Utah is playing well enough to win more than this
